O relativo no dativo e com preposição, p: The relative pronoun in the dative and with prepositions, step by step
PASSO 1: se o relativo é OBJETO INDIRETO: STEP 1: if the relative pronoun is an INDIRECT OBJECT, it goes into the DATIVE: «dem» (m), «der» (f), «dem» (n), «DENEN» (plural — a form of its own!). STEP 2: the same goes if a PREPOSITION that takes the dative comes before it: «Der Mann, mit dem ich spreche, ist mein Chef» (the man I'm talking to / with whom I'm talking). STEP 3: RULE: the PREPOSITION goes BEFORE the relative pronoun — never at the end, as English allows ("the man I'm talking to"): «mit dem», «in der», «in dem», «mit denen», «bei dem». STEP 4: the CASE of the relative pronoun is whatever the preposition takes: «mit» + dative → «mit dem»; «für» + accusative → «für den»; «in» + Wo? dative → «in der». STEP 5: forms: «Die Stadt, in der ich wohne» (the city I live in), «Das Haus, in dem ich lebe», «Die Freunde, mit denen ich reise» (the friends I travel with), «Der Verein, bei dem ich Mitglied bin» (the club I'm a member of).
o português diz «o homem com quem falo»: Everyday English leaves the preposition dangling at the end: "the city I live in", "the friends I travel with". Formal English puts it in front: "the city in which I live", "the friends with whom I travel" — and that formal version is the ONLY one German allows: «die Stadt, in der ich wohne», «die Freunde, mit denen ich reise».

Relativas com preposições do acusativo e: Relative clauses with accusative and two-way prepositions
PASSO 1: preposições que pedem ACUSATIVO: STEP 1: prepositions that take the ACCUSATIVE use «den, die, das, die»: «Die Frau, für die ich arbeite, ist nett» (the woman I work for). «Das Thema, über das wir sprechen, ist wichtig» (the topic we're talking about). STEP 2: two-way prepositions with movement: «Der Berg, auf den wir steigen, ist hoch» (the mountain we're climbing). STEP 3: verbs with a fixed preposition also create relative clauses: «Der Film, auf den ich mich freue, beginnt um acht» (the movie I'm looking forward to — sich freuen auf + Akk); «Das Buch, von dem ich dir erzählt habe …» (the book I told you about — erzählen von + Dat). STEP 4: remember: the verb's fixed preposition decides the case.

Dessen e deren: o relativo de posse: Dessen and deren: the possessive relative
PASSO 1: para indicar POSSE dentro da re: STEP 1: to show POSSESSION inside a relative clause — English "whose" — German uses «DESSEN» (masculine and neuter) and «DEREN» (feminine and plural). STEP 2: the owner comes before; the thing owned comes after, with NO article: «Der Mann, dessen Auto dort steht, ist mein Nachbar» (the man whose car is parked there is my neighbor). STEP 3: «Die Frau, deren Tochter Ärztin ist, wohnt hier» (the woman whose daughter is a doctor lives here). STEP 4: «Das Kind, dessen Mutter arbeitet, geht in die Schule.» «Die Leute, deren Kinder spielen, sind meine Freunde.» STEP 5: the conjugated verb goes to the end. Note: English "whose" never changes; German chooses by the OWNER's gender: dessen (him/it), deren (her/them).
